annotation.title_clean: Not Relational Enough? Towards an Eco-Relational Approach in Robot Ethics
annotation.title_en: Not Relational Enough? Towards an Eco-Relational Approach in Robot Ethics
annotation.summary_en: Philosophical article arguing robot ethics is not relational enough. It critiques the properties approach and modestly relational approaches, and proposes an eco-relational, phenomenological approach that anchors autonomy, agency and responsibility in relations with non-human entities such as animals and robots, implying hybrid actions and non-human agency.
key_provisions_or_claims: Dominant robot ethics approaches presuppose human-only properties like consciousness and intelligence.
Proposes an eco-relational approach embedding relationality with non-humans in ethical concepts from the outset.
Human properties and actions are co-accomplishments with non-human entities, including robots.
Introduces hybrid actions and non-human agency, disrupting traditional ethical concepts.
Draws on environmental ethics and African and East Asian relational traditions.
